report:
COMPARISON:None.

CLINICAL HISTORY:Fall, subsequent swelling left knee. Suspected meniscal tear.

PROCEDURE:Multisequence, multiplanar unenhanced MRI of the left knee according to routine protocol.

IMAGING FINDINGS:

Nondiagnostic scout localizing images reviewed.

The lateral meniscus is intact. The medial meniscus is intact.

Intact anterior cruciate ligament and posterior cruciate ligament.

The medial collateral ligament, posterior oblique ligament, fibular collateral ligament, popliteus and biceps femoris tendon attachments, as well as iliotibial band are intact.

The patellar retinacula are intact. No femoral trochlear dysplasia. The TT-TG distance measures 12 mm, within normal limits. The quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact.

There is fissuring of articular cartilage along the patellar apex and lateral patellar facet. Trochlear articular cartilage is preserved. Medial and lateral femorotibial articular cartilage is preserved. Focal full thickness cartilage denuding posterior nonweightbearing aspect lateral femoral condyle.

Trace knee joint fluid. Small Baker's cyst. Regional musculature is within normal limits. 

IMPRESSION:
1. No evidence of discrete meniscal tear.
2. Mild to moderate patellofemoral chondrosis suggesting evolving patellofemoral osteoarthritis.

Technique: MRI of the knee. Results: Complete tear of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus with subluxation, full-thickness cartilage loss in the medial compartment with subchondral edema and cyst, early degeneration of the lateral and patellofemoral compartments, joint effusion, and mild synovitis. Conclusion: Complete medial meniscus tear with subluxation, advanced chondromalacia of the medial compartment, early osteoarthritis of lateral and patellofemoral compartments, joint effusion, and synovitis.

Mediales Kompartiment:
Regelrechtes Knochenmarksignal. Geringe Irregularität des Knorpel an der medialen Femurcondyle mit aber intakter Grenzlamelle (Serie 4/ Image 21) (Outerbridge Grad 2). Intakter Innenmeniskus. Intaktes MCL.

Laterales Kompartiment:
Regelrechtes Knochenmarksignal. Intakter Knorpel. Intakter Außenmeniskus. Intaktes LCL.

Femoropatellares Gleitlager und Patella:
Regelrechtes Knochenmarksignal. Intakter Knorpel. Regelrechtes Lig. patellae. [DATE].

Kreuzbänder:
[DATE]. In der ehemaligen Rupturzone wirkt das VKB noch narbig aufgetrieben. Keine größere verbliebene Banddehiszenz oder stark dislozierte bandanteile. Intaktes HKB.

Muskulatur und übrige Weichteile:
Geringer Kniegelenkerguss. Regelrechtes flow void in den miterfassten Gefäßen.

Findings:  There is a minimal knee effusion. Normal medial and lateral menisci. No evidence of tears.  Normal ACL, PCL, MCL and LCL. Normal extensor mechanism.  Mild fraying of the medial compartment articular cartilage is noted. The lateral compartment articular cartilage is preserved. There is severe thinning and loss of the patellar ridge and lateral patellar facet articular cartilage. Normal trochlear articular cartilage.  
Conclusion: No meniscal tears. Medial compartment and patellar articular cartilage degeneration noted.

MCL proximal gering narbig verbreitert bei stattgehabter Läsion [DATE] (5/17). VKB distal mukoid mit regredient vorgewölbten Anteil, aktuell durchgängig abgrenzbar. Meniscen teils mukoid signalalteriert (führend IM-HH), aktuell ohne sichere Rissbildung. Geringe Gonarthrose mit überwiegend oberflächlichen Chondropathien. Geringe Retropatellararthrose. Enthesiopathie der Quadrizepssehne am Patellaoberpol. Kein Gelenkerguss, kein Knochenödem oder bone bruise.

Technique: MRI of the right knee. Results: Test report. MCL normal. ACL normal. Medial meniscus degenerative changes grade 2. Lateral meniscus normal. Mild chondromalacia of medial compartment.  No baker's cyst. Impression: Medial meniscus degenerative changes grade 2. Mild chondromalacia of medial compartments.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Bilateral inner knee pain for several years.
Comparison: Knee radiographs dated [DATE]

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
No joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. Small, ruptured Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Normal morphology with mild intrasubstance myxoid degeneration. No medial meniscus tear.
Medial compartment cartilage: Moderate grade partial-thickness cartilage loss at the weightbearing medial femoral condyle. Cartilage on the medial tibial plateau is preserved.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
There is moderate grade partial-thickness cartilage loss at the patellar median ridge, with mild chondral fissuring at the medial and lateral patellar facets.
Mild chondral edema and heterogeneity at the femoral trochlea.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: Mild insertional quadriceps tendinosis with intrasubstance degeneration at its medial margin attachment to the patella. No tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 15 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
1.	Patellofemoral and medial tibiofemoral compartment chondrosis.
2.	Mild insertional quadriceps tendinosis.

MRI LEFT KNEE  (plain)

Clinical information:
1.3 cm lesion at the left femur observed on MRI performed on [Date], recommended follow-up in 6 months.

Technique: 
Multiplanar MR of the knee according to protocol.

Comparison: 
None

Findings: 

Menisci

Lateral meniscus: intact

Medial meniscus: intact

Ligaments

Anterior cruciate ligament: intact

Posterior cruciate ligament: intact 

Medial collateral ligament: Superficial and deep components intact. No periligamentous edema.

Lateral collateral ligament: The iliotibial band, biceps femoris tendon, fibular collateral ligament and popliteus muscle and tendon intact. 

Posterolateral corner structures: Intact

Extensor Mechanism

The distal quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact. The patella is normally positioned within the femoral groove. There is no retinacular disruption.

Fluid

No joint effusion or loose body. No Baker's cyst.

Osseous and Articular Structures

Bones: Previously observed T2 weighted bright lesion located at the anteromedial distal femoral metadiaphysis shows no significant interval change in size. It currently measures approximately 1.1 cm x 1.4 cm x 1.6 cm in size. It has lobulated margins that shows a narrow zone of transition. No adjacent marrow edema is seen. No abnormal soft tissue component, cortical break nor abnormal periosteal reaction detected. Imaging findings are highly suggestive of a nonaggressive bony lesion, top differential diagnoses include a small bone cyst or a small or intraosseous ganglion. Interval increase in edema is also seen at the anterior medial tibia close to the insertion of the meniscal root, possibly due to traction or intraosseous ganglion. No fracture, stress reaction, or other osseous lesion is seen.

Patellofemoral compartment: Mild chondrosis of the medial patella facet.

Medial compartment: Minimal chondrosis.

Lateral compartment: Mild chondrosis.

Others:

Hoffa's fat pad: clear

Muscles: No abnormal oedema. 

Neurovascular bundle: Normal 


COMMENT
Previously described T2 weighted bright lesion at the anterior aspect of the distal femoral metadiaphysis shows no significant with change compared with prior study, probably represents a nonaggressive lesion such as a small bone cyst or an intraosseous ganglion.

Minimal to mild chondrosis of the tibiofemoral joint and patellofemoral joint are similar to prior study.

Interval increase in edema is seen at the anteromedial tibia adjacent to the insertion of the anterior medial meniscal root, may represent an intraosseous ganglion.

Partialläsion des MCL bei durchgängig erhaltener Bandstruktur jedoch deutlich vermehrt umgebender Flüssigkeit. Deutlich Knochenmarködem in der ventrolateralen Femurkondyle am Ansatz des Tractus iliotibialis und anterolateralen Bandes und umgebend Flüssigkeit zum Tractus iliotibialis ohne fassbare Diskontinuität der Bandstrukturen DD bei Partialläsion. Gelenkerguss. Mukoide Degeneration des Innenmeniskus im Pars intermedia und Hinterhorn ohne Rissbildung. Oberflächliche retropatellare Chondropathie. Darüber hinaus keine wesentliche Chondropathie. Diskretes subchondrales Knochenmarködem im dorsomedialen Tibiaplateau DD a.e. degenerativ.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Several months of pain in the suprapatellar region.
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.2 Tesla open system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
No joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. Small, multiloculated Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Vertical tear of the peripheral posterior horn/body junction without extrusion. No flipped fragments. No parameniscal cyst.
Medial compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear. Edema within the anterior suprapatellar fat pad.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 7 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
1.	Vertical tear of the medial meniscus peripheral posterior horn without extrusion.
2.	Edema within the anterior suprapatellar fat pad, could represent fat pad impingement.
